summary: L2J Mobius is a mature, actively-developed Java Lineage 2 server emulator. Its Interlude (Chronicle C6, protocol 746) build lives at repo path L2J_Mobius_CT_0_Interlude. It uses a classic LoginServer + GameServer split, an Ant build, Java 25, and MySQL/MariaDB via HikariCP. The rewritten codebase roots at package org.l2jmobius, with the actor model under gameserver.entity.actor (Creature -> Npc/Playable -> Player/Attackable). NPC AI is Java-based (AbstractAI/CreatureAI/AttackableAI) driven by per-second AttackableThinkTaskManager pools plus a MovementTaskManager; datapack AI scripts are Java files compiled at runtime by ScriptEngine. Crucially for L3, the server ALREADY ships two synthetic-population mechanisms we can hook: (1) a full "Fake Player" system where synthetic players are modeled as NPCs that broadcast a FakePlayerInfo packet so clients render them as real players, and (2) AutoPlayTaskManager + OfflinePlay which drive REAL Player objects autonomously (server-side auto-hunt bot). License is transitioning from GPLv3 to MIT per-file. This is a solid, buildable core for L3.
key_facts: Repository: https://gitlab.com/MobiusDevelopment/L2J_Mobius , single 'master' branch, ~11,900 commits, one monorepo folder per chronicle. Interlude project path: L2J_Mobius_CT_0_Interlude (folder-per-chronicle, NOT a git branch).

Client protocol: AllowedProtocolRevisions = 746 (confirmed in dist/game/config/Server.ini) - this is Interlude / Chronicle C6 as expected. ProtocolVersion.java client packet validates against ServerConfig.PROTOCOL_LIST; value -2 is a C2 ping that gets disconnected.

Architecture: separate LoginServer + GameServer processes. Entry classes org.l2jmobius.loginserver.LoginServer and org.l2jmobius.gameserver.GameServer; GameServer connects to LoginServer via gameserver/LoginServerThread.java. Build produces LoginServer.jar, GameServer.jar, DatabaseInstaller.jar.
Java version: Java 25 REQUIRED. build.xml sets javac source=25 target=25, compiler='modern', and a checkRequirements target fails with 'Java 25 is required.' Ant >= 1.8.2 needed.
Build system: Apache Ant (build.xml per project). No Maven/Gradle. Output packaged as L2J_Mobius_CT_0_Interlude.zip via adding-core -> adding-datapack -> adding-readme -> cleanup targets.

Database: MySQL/MariaDB. Bundled libs are HikariCP-7.0.2 (JDBC connection pool) and mysql-connector-j-9.5.0 (driver), plus slf4j-2.0.17. DB config in dist/game/config/Database.ini; schema installed via DatabaseInstaller.jar (org.l2jmobius.tools.DatabaseInstaller) and dist/db_installer SQL. Connection pooling code in org.l2jmobius.commons.database.

Package root is org.l2jmobius. Source layout: commons (shared: config, crypt, database, network, threads, time, ui, util), gameserver, loginserver, log, tools. Note this is the REWRITTEN layout - actors live under gameserver.entity.actor, NOT the legacy gameserver.model.actor.

Actor/object model (gameserver.entity.actor): WorldObject (in gameserver.entity) -> Creature -> { Npc, Playable, Vehicle, ... }. Npc -> Attackable (monsters). Playable -> Player and Summon. World model: gameserver.entity.World, WorldRegion, Location, WorldObject. Concrete NPC subtypes in gameserver.entity.actor.instance: Monster, RaidBoss, GrandBoss, Guard, Merchant, Pet, Servitor, Defender, etc.

Player representation: org.l2jmobius.gameserver.entity.actor.Player (this is the PcInstance equivalent; the legacy 'PcInstance' name is gone in this rewrite). Player extends Playable extends Creature. A Player is bound to its network connection via GameClient.setPlayer/getPlayer, guarded by a ReentrantLock.

NPC/monster AI is JAVA-based (not Lua/Python). Core classes in gameserver.ai: AbstractAI, CreatureAI, AttackableAI (monster combat), PlayerAI, PlayableAI, SummonAI, SiegeGuardAI, DoorAI, BoatAI. AI uses an Intention enum (IDLE/ACTIVE/ATTACK/CAST/MOVE_TO/FOLLOW...) and setIntention* methods. AttackableAI.notifyActionThink() switches on intention -> thinkActive/thinkAttack/thinkCast. Aggro scan via World.forEachVisibleObject + isAggressiveTowards; _globalAggro ramps 0..N to delay aggro after spawn.

AI ticking / threading model: AttackableThinkTaskManager holds Attackable NPCs in Set<Set<Attackable>> POOLS with POOL_SIZE=1000; each pool runs its own task every TASK_DELAY=1000ms via ThreadPool.schedulePriorityTaskAtFixedRate, calling ai.notifyActionThink() per NPC (self-pruning when AI is null). Movement handled separately by MovementTaskManager. ~19 task managers total in gameserver.taskmanagers. Thread pool is org.l2jmobius.commons.threads.ThreadPool (with ThreadPriority, ThreadProvider).

Datapack AI scripts: dist/game/data/scripts/ contains ai/ (subfolders areas, bosses, others), quests/, handlers/, events/, village_master/, vehicles/, custom/. Individual NPC AIs are .java files (e.g. FleeMonsters.java, TurekOrcs.java). Loaded/compiled at runtime by gameserver.scripting.ScriptEngine, which scans .java files (exclusions from config/Scripts.xml) and delegates to gameserver.scripting.engine.ScriptExecutor. Uses annotations (gameserver.scripting.annotations).

SYNTHETIC PLAYER MECHANISM #1 - Fake Players (model synthetic players AS NPCs): Enabled via dist/game/config/Custom/FakePlayers.ini (EnableFakePlayers=False default, plus FakePlayerChat, FakePlayerUseShots, FakePlayerAggroMonsters, FakePlayerCanDropItems/Pickup, PvP/karma reward flags). Implemented as a flag on the NPC template: Npc.isFakePlayer() reads NpcTemplate.isFakePlayer(); NpcTemplate.getFakePlayerInfo() returns a FakePlayerHolder. Key hook: Npc.sendInfo()/updateAbnormalEffect() sends a FakePlayerInfo server packet (instead of normal NpcInfo) so the CLIENT renders them as real players. Chat lines in data/FakePlayerChatData.xml. Config class: FakePlayersConfig (e.g. FAKE_PLAYER_USE_SHOTS).

SYNTHETIC PLAYER MECHANISM #2 - AutoPlay / OfflinePlay (drive REAL Player objects): gameserver.taskmanagers.AutoPlayTaskManager is a built-in server-side auto-hunt bot. Pools of up to 200 real Players, task every 700ms; selects targets via World.getNearestVisibleObjectInRange and issues player.getAI().setIntentionAttack(target) / setIntentionMoveTo, does doPickupItem, sweep/spoil (skill 254), party assist. Config Custom/AutoPlay.ini. OfflinePlay (Custom/OfflinePlay.ini, .offlineplay command) keeps a real Player in-world auto-playing after client disconnect, persistable across restarts. Also OfflineTrade.ini and OnlineInfo.ini (EnableOnlineCommand) exist.

Network layer: CUSTOM NIO framework in org.l2jmobius.commons.network (NOT Netty, NOT the old MMOCore). GameClient extends commons.network.Client<Connection<GameClient>>; uses ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer (commons.network.buffer). Blowfish/XOR encryption via network.Encryption + BlowFishKeygen. ConnectionState flow: CONNECTED -> AUTHENTICATED -> ENTERING -> IN_GAME -> DISCONNECTED. Client packets in gameserver.network.clientpackets (ProtocolVersion, AuthLogin, CharacterSelect, EnterWorld, Action, AttackRequest, MoveToLocation...); server packets in serverpackets; packet dispatch via GamePacketHandler + ClientPackets/ExClientPackets enums; each packet's runImpl(player) executes on the ThreadPool.
Scale target: dist/game/config/Server.ini sets MaximumOnlineUsers = 2000 (design capacity for a single GameServer instance for this Interlude build).

License: transitioning from GPLv3 to MIT. Per the README, all NEW and REWRITTEN code is MIT; not-yet-rewritten files remain GPLv3, and the per-file header governs. A distribution containing any GPLv3 file must be treated as GPLv3 as a whole until the rewrite completes.
architecture_notes: Base L3 on the L2J_Mobius_CT_0_Interlude folder as the server core; keep the LoginServer/GameServer split and the org.l2jmobius package root. Our synthetic-player layer plugs into gameserver.entity.actor (Player) and the taskmanagers, not into the network client.

Two viable synthetic-player designs already exist in-tree, and we should pick deliberately: (A) 'Fake Player as NPC' - cheapest, scales to thousands, they are Npc/Attackable objects broadcast to clients via the FakePlayerInfo packet so they LOOK like players; but they are NOT real Players (no inventory/skills/party semantics unless we add them). (B) 'AutoPlay/OfflinePlay on real Player' - full-fidelity synthetic players that are genuine Player objects the server drives via their AI; heavier (each is a full Player) but automatically produces valid client state everywhere. L3 likely wants a hybrid: real Player fidelity where interaction matters, fake-NPC cheapness for ambient crowd/online-count.

AI is a clean extension point: NPC behavior = Java AI classes (AttackableAI) + Java datapack scripts compiled by ScriptEngine. To give synthetic players richer behavior than the stock AutoPlayTaskManager, we can either add a new task manager (mirroring AttackableThinkTaskManager's pooled 1s-tick pattern) or write datapack AI scripts. Reuse the Intention state machine (setIntentionAttack/MoveTo/Cast) rather than inventing a new control API.

Threading budget is explicit and poolable: NPC think = 1000ms tick, AutoPlay = 700ms tick, both via ThreadPool.schedulePriorityTaskAtFixedRate with fixed-size pools (1000 NPCs / 200 players per pool). Any L3 synthetic-player controller should follow the same pooled-fixed-rate model to stay within the shared ThreadPool and to keep per-tick work bounded. Budget against MaximumOnlineUsers=2000 as the single-instance real-player ceiling.

Client state validity: because the custom commons.network layer plus the clientpackets/serverpackets pair define the wire protocol, real-Player synthetic characters (design B) inherit correct packet emission for free. Fake-NPC synthetic players (design A) only emit what Npc.sendInfo() sends (FakePlayerInfo + movement/effects) - if L3 needs them to appear in party/trade/community-board contexts, those packets/paths must be added explicitly.

Build/runtime baseline for L3: Java 25 toolchain, Ant, MySQL/MariaDB with HikariCP. Adopt these as project prerequisites; the DatabaseInstaller tool defines the schema we extend for any persisted synthetic-player state (compare OfflinePlay's 'store to database / restore after restart' as a template).
risks: License ambiguity: the codebase is mid-migration GPLv3 -> MIT. Until the rewrite is complete, a full distribution must be treated as GPLv3 (copyleft: derivative works must be open-sourced under GPL). L3 cannot assume MIT for the whole tree - we must audit per-file headers of every file we reuse/modify. This is a real legal constraint on whether L3 can be closed-source or commercial.

The 'Fake Player' system is designed as ambient NPCs, not full players - the config comment says they 'operate seamlessly like NPCs.' They likely lack real inventory, skill casting fidelity, party/clan membership, and Community Board presence. If L3 needs synthetic players indistinguishable from humans in ALL systems, mechanism A will need substantial extension.

AutoPlayTaskManager drives REAL Player objects - each synthetic player of design B carries the full memory/CPU cost of a Player (stats, status, inventory, effects, region visibility). Scaling to large synthetic populations this way could blow past the 2000-user single-instance design ceiling; needs load testing.

Datapack AI scripts are compiled at runtime by ScriptExecutor (mechanism not fully confirmed from ScriptEngine.java alone - likely javax.tools JavaCompiler or ECJ inside gameserver.scripting.engine). Runtime Java compilation adds startup cost and a JDK (not just JRE) dependency; worth confirming ScriptExecutor internals before relying heavily on script hot-loading.

GitLab web UI is JS-rendered and does not return content to WebFetch; and the blob-search API requires auth (401). All findings here came from the unauthenticated REST tree API + raw file endpoints. A few internals (ScriptExecutor compilation method, exact FakePlayerHolder fields, FakePlayerInfo packet contents) were inferred from references and not read line-by-line; verify against a local clone.

This is Interlude/C6 (protocol 746) - an old client. If L3's ambitions need modern client features, note that Mobius also ships newer chronicles (High Five CT_2.6, GrandCrusade, etc.) with the same architecture; the synthetic-player work would port but the actor/packet details differ.
recommendations: Clone the repo locally (into c:\Agentic per the working-directory constraint) and pin to a specific commit; do NOT rely on GitLab WebFetch for ongoing development - the tree API works but raw-file reads are the only reliable content path. Read the actual files: Player.java, Npc.java, AttackableAI.java, AutoPlayTaskManager.java, ScriptExecutor.java, and the FakePlayerHolder/FakePlayerInfo packet.

For L3 synthetic players, prototype BOTH mechanisms against a running server: (A) enable FakePlayers.ini and observe how fake-NPC players render/behave client-side; (B) enable AutoPlay.ini + OfflinePlay.ini and observe real-Player auto-hunt. This directly informs whether L3 builds on the NPC path (scale) or the Player path (fidelity), or a hybrid.

Model the L3 synthetic-player controller after AttackableThinkTaskManager: pooled fixed-size collections, single fixed-rate ThreadPool task per pool, per-entity think() dispatch, self-pruning. Reuse the existing Intention API (setIntentionAttack/MoveTo/Cast) instead of a parallel control system.

Do a license audit BEFORE committing to reuse: grep every file we touch for its header (MIT vs GPLv3) and decide L3's own license accordingly. If L3 must be non-GPL, restrict reuse to MIT-headered files or plan a clean-room reimplementation of GPL-only pieces.

Set up the toolchain now: JDK 25, Ant, MariaDB/MySQL + HikariCP, run DatabaseInstaller to stand up the schema. Establish a build of the stock Interlude server as the baseline before layering L3 changes.

Confirm ScriptExecutor's runtime-compilation approach and startup cost early, since L3 NPC/synthetic-player behaviors may be authored as datapack Java scripts - this determines whether hot-reloading behaviors is feasible.
open_questions: What exactly does ScriptExecutor (gameserver.scripting.engine.ScriptExecutor) use to compile the .java datapack scripts at runtime - javax.tools.JavaCompiler, Eclipse ECJ, or precompiled loading? This affects the JDK-vs-JRE requirement and hot-reload capability.

What fields does FakePlayerHolder carry and what does the FakePlayerInfo server packet actually serialize (equipment, class, title, clan)? Determines how convincingly fake-NPC players appear to clients and what L3 must add.

Are fake players spawned via the normal SpawnTable/spawns XML (as NPC templates flagged isFakePlayer) or by a dedicated manager? We saw no FakePlayers folder under data/scripts/ai, so the spawn/management path needs locating in the codebase.
How many synthetic players (design B, real Players) can one GameServer sustain in practice relative to the 2000 real-user design target? Requires load testing.
Does the Interlude Player support the same AutoUse/AutoPotion/AutoUseTaskManager automation that newer chronicles have, and how complete is party/summon auto-play for synthetic players?

For L3's goals specifically (not stated in this task), which matters more - synthetic-player SCALE (favor fake-NPC) or full-system FIDELITY (favor real-Player)? This drives the core architecture choice.
